  Regular Meeting Minutes
  September 14, 2023

CALL TO ORDER - Chair Flores called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m.

FLAG SALUTE - by Vice Chair Ruiz

ROLL CALL - by Ana Medina, Sr. Secretary
Present: Chair Alan Flores, Vice Chair Lizette Ruiz, Commissioners Edgar Pelayo and Adolfo Varas.
Secretary Jennifer Cypert had an excused absence.
Staff: Director Steve Costley, Deputy Director Tina Fierro, Parks Superintendent Glenn Massey, and
Recreation Supervisor James Markel.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES FOR: JULY 13, 2023 & AUGUST 10, 2023:
Recommended Motion: Motion to approve the minutes as presented
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/ Vice Chair Ruiz ; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was unanimously
approved; for the July minutes
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/ Commissioner Varas; a roll call vote was taken, and motion was
unanimously approved; for the August minutes

Recognized: Mr. Dominguez, a South Gate resident, asked why minutes were needed for August 10 when
a meeting wasn’t held; Director Costley explained they are needed for the record.

PUBLIC COMMENT - None

PRESENTATION: - None

OPEN SESSION ITEMS
1. HALLOWEEN EVENTS 2023
Recommended Motion: Receive and file.
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/ Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Deputy Dir. Fierro reviewed this item. It was suggested to use glow items to give away; a discussion ensued.

2. SPORTS & AQUATICS DIVISION REPORT
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Chair Flores/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously approved.
James Markel, Recreation Supervisor reviewed these items; a discussion ensued.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, a South Gate resident, asked how can they teach surfing on dry land; Mr.
Markel explained the basics and techniques are taught on dry land. He also asked why is archery not taught,
Director Costley explained the safety issues.
Vice Chair Ruiz asked about women's basketball. Commissioner Pelayo asked what is on the Division's wish list,
Recreation Supv. Markel replied he would like to see a pickleball court, more aquatic programs, and advanced
recreation programs.

3. MAJOR PROJECTS UPDATES
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file

  4
 M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Director Costley reviewed this item. A discussion ensued.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, a South Gate resident, asked if staff applied for congressional funding for
Hollydale Community Park and to be given a date it would be completed, Director Costley replied they
had but didn't qualify. Guarantees can't be given for construction completion dates; due to the foreman
passing away there have been delays. The Urban Orchard estimated completion date is November 2024.
Vice Chair Ruiz asked about the fence project; Director Costley explained the process. Commissioner
Pelayo asked about the Boy Scouts huts; Director Costley replied about what could be done.

4. RECREATION DIVISION 4TH QUARTER REPORT FY 2022/23
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Vice Chair Ruiz/Commissioner Pelayo; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Deputy Dir. Fierro reviewed this item, a discussion ensued. Chair Varas asked if the Art Association was asked
to participate in the Art Walk event; Director Costley explained that they are currently restructuring.

5. GROUNDS & FACILITY DIVISION 4TH QUARTER REPORT FY 2022/23
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, a South Gate resident, asked if flowers could be planted in Triangle Park,
Parks Supt. Massey replied there's a problem with vandals and transients, but they are planning on
planting more plants.
Parks Supt. Massey reviewed this item, he explained that during the summer not a lot of projects are
done since staff is mostly concentrating on maintenance because of the high use of the Parks. A
discussion ensued.

6. REVIEW OF FY2022/23 FEE WAIVERS
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Commissioner Varas/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Director Costley reported on this item, a discussion ensued. Commissioner Pelayo asked why LAUSD
receives fee waivers; Director Costley explained the process for fee waivers.

7. REPORT ON AZTEC YOUTH FOOTBALL
Recommended Motion: Motion to receive and file
M/S/C: Commissioner Pelayo/Vice Chair Ruiz; a roll call vote was taken; motion was unanimously
approved.
Director Costley reviewed this item, a discussion ensued.
Recognized: Mario Dominguez, a South Gate resident, asked about the snack bar revenue, Director

September 28 at 3:00 p.m. The memorial service for former Council Member De Witt will be September
24. The Centennial Car Show will be held Sunday, September 30 at the Golf Course. The annual Art Walk

   Parks & Recreation Commission Regular Meeting
  November 9, 2023
  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 2
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Tina De La Rosa, Deputy Director of Parks & Rec.
Date:  October 12, 2023
Subject:  Recreation Programing Report – 1st Quarter Review FY 2023/24

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Aquatics:
Summer season brought back the return of Sunrise Swim and Moonlight Lagoon on
weekdays. Additional pool time was offered during weekdays for adults from 6-7:30am
and 9-9:45pm. On Fridays, we offered an additional Family Swim hour at night to beat
the heat. We maxed our attendance for most Family Swim sessions (200-250 people
per session). On weekends, we were sold out every Saturday and Sunday night for
party rentals.

As for programs, we offered group, private and semi-private swim lessons for all
ages. In total, we taught approximately 2,100 patrons how to swim and how to be water
safe. Almost 1,200 of those registrations were for group lessons, approximately 700 of
them were kids, ages 6-17; 270 of them were Tiny Tots, ages 3-5; 150 Parent & Child
lessons, and about 55 adults. Close to 450 of those registrations were for private and
semi-private lessons, almost 300 of those for youth ages 6-17; over 100 for Tiny Tots;
and almost 25 for adults. Once again, we partnered with the LA84 Foundation, who
generously gifted us a grant of almost $23K to provide swimming lessons for over 500
underprivileged kids. We offered specialized programs such as Gators Swim Academy,
Junior Lifeguard, and Surf Academy for Teens. These programs are designed for older,
more advanced kids looking to physically challenge themselves and cultivate their
leadership skills. Our Pre-Competitive Swim Class and Junior Water Polo, both great
feeder programs, were a huge success with over 60 registrations. Aquatics Staff were
also very proud to present our first ever Summer Splash Camp for kids, geared at
providing water safety but also to increase awareness of the variety of aquatic sports
offered such as diving, water polo, and surfing. Activities included throwing water

  Page 1 of 4
  10
 balloons, playing volleyball and basketball in the pool, and a multitude of other aquatics
games. The Summer Splash Camp was a success with over 70 registrants!

We again partnered with the World’s Largest Swimming Lesson to spread the message
that “swimming lessons save lives.” Our free event was sponsored by Partner
Organization SG Aquatics Club and we had almost 200 people in attendance. Our free
Community Swim Days returned. We hosted a Summer Kick Off Splash event in June,
a 4th of July Splash event, and a Back-to-School Splash event in August. We reached
approximately 100 people in attendance per event and had a variety of activities for
families to enjoy on the lawn and in the pool.

Fitness:
Our first quarter tends to be one of our busiest. This year was no different. We
sold/renewed a total of 3,592 memberships. That is up by nearly 600 memberships
since the previous quarter. Our most popular option continues to be the Fitness
Membership, specifically the Adult option. Additionally, our Premier membership tier
saw a 40% increase in purchases/renewals. This isn’t surprising to see during the
summer months as many members upgrade to have access to the Swim Stadium.

Despite the rise in Memberships, Daily Admissions stayed steady with the previous
quarter. We typically see an inverse effect between Memberships and Daily
Admissions, but this quarter showed a different trend. We had 2,889 Daily Admissions;
with 1,244 coming from the Adult Sports option, which is limited to only basketball court
use.

Personal Training has stayed consistent with 180 hours of training conducted. The
Private 12 session package continues to be the most popular option. This tends to be
one of our slowest seasons for Personal Training due to the Biggest Loser Challenge, in
which many of our Personal Training clients participate.

We also held our second annual Fun Run on Saturday, July 15. We had 850 registered
runners, plus a few hundred spectators. Each registered runner received a sack pack,
sunglasses, t-shirt, and cooling towel. The one-mile route consisted of inflatable
obstacle courses with water slides, a mud pit, slime zones, foam, and plenty of wet
zones. The event culminated with a large raffle of gift cards, and items donated by our
gracious sponsors and donors.

The Sports Center and Swim Stadium will undergo a long overdue audio system
upgrade. The upgrade will provide clear and consistent audio for all exercise rooms at
the Sports Center. It will also allow us to introduce the new and innovative trend of
virtual fitness classes on a projector and bring more value to our membership

  Page 2 of 4
  11
 program. Additionally, the audio system will have a public address function, which can
be utilized for critical announcements and emergencies. We estimate the upgrade will
be completed by December 2023.

Youth Sports
Our first quarter started off with all youth fundamental sport classes filled to capacity.
Due to the high demand for summer classes, we were able to expand class capacity to
20 participants per class. Our core group (basketball, volleyball, baseball, multi-sport,
and soccer) of fundamental classes continue to be popular and provides introductory
drills and lessons to the aforementioned sports. Contract classes were also in high
demand this summer, karate and tennis had increases in total number of participants.
Karate also hosted their annual Do-Shito International Karate Tournament which
welcomed competitors from Nicaragua, El Salvador, and local talent. The event was
well attended with over 150 competitors and 500 spectators. Lastly, our brand-new Rec
on the Run (mobile recreation program) has concluded. The program was conducted bi-
weekly with events scheduled at Cesar Chavez and Hollydale Regional Parks. Drop-in
participation averaged between 30-40 people during the 3-7pm time frame.

Adult Sports:
Our first quarter of Adult Sports ended on a high note with our Men’s and Co-ed Softball
teams wrapping up with new champions crowned. This season brought in 35 total
teams across 6 divisions who battled weekly for the top spot. Champions were awarded
the newly re-designed Championship hoodies while 2nd place winners received their
customized insulated South Gate water bottles. Our Fall season began immediately at
the conclusion of the previous season; we currently have 36 teams enrolled (18 Men’s -
3 divisions & 18 Co-ed - 3 divisions). Open play volleyball has remained popular on
Tuesday evenings and brought in over 725 drop-in participants this quarter. We are
currently in the recruiting stage for the next Men’s and Women’s basketball leagues.

Partner Organizations:
SG Aztecs have begun their regular season practices and games. The Aztecs currently
have 7 football teams and 5 cheer teams that serve nearly 300 youth.
SGJAA concluded their summer basketball league with their traditional all-star games
and team banquets. Fall baseball and softball have commenced; JAA is currently
conducting games and practices every day of the week.
AYSO has officially begun their Fall season and are currently hosting practices at
Hollydale Regional Park Monday through Thursday with games played on Saturdays.

Social Media:
Our total followers are now up to 4,605. Last quarter we had 8 posts, and 115 stories.
We have reached over 16,000 accounts and engaged with 1,416. We continue to

  Page 3 of 4
  12
 recruit a Recreation Marketing Coordinator to oversee the Social Media Task Force and
all social media outlets.

Youth Programs
All dance classes along with Tumbling and Cheerleading are at maximum capacity. We
had 12 different art classes available, and all classes were full the first week of
registration. Tot Time registrations have increased to an average of 20 per class and
four Tiny Twos classes filled fast. Staff coordinated an excursion for preschoolers and
their parents to Wild Rivers, both dates were filled to 100 participants.

Senior Programs
There were 10 trips scheduled for Summer and all were filled with 50 patrons on each.
The HSA lunch program continues to grow in attendance and the social activities are
increasing as well. The Blue Jays are still practicing their dancing skills three times a
week and have accepted new participants.

Cultural Arts
The Museum/Art Gallery hosted the first Zine event on August 12. Staff coordinated lots
of activities, history, shops, and trade zines. The opening reception for the Art Exhibit
“Process/Proceso” was also on display and would be on display until October. Staff
started an Art Club for two different age groups, and both were very well attended.

Special Events
Concerts in the Park took place each Friday in July at 6pm in the Bandstand area. The
last concert which featured the Mariachi Divas also had food trucks and a beer garden
as part of the Centennial celebration. Movies in the Park took place each Friday in
August at 8pm in the Golf Course. On September 8 we held a Teen Glow event to try to
increase teen activities in the Park. There were 130 teens in attendance since staff
invited neighboring cities that have Teen Centers to attend. Only 30 teens wee from
South Gate. They enjoyed laser tag, food, drinks, glow golf and fun glow items to wear
were handed out to all in attendance.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 3
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  October 19, 2023
Subject:  Grounds & Parks Facility Maintenance - 1st Quarter Review FY
  2023/24

Recommended Motion: Motion to Receive and File

Grounds Maintenance
On Saturday July 29th the SELA Arts Festival Event took place on the LA River adjacent
to Hollydale Regional Park.

We continue to suppress the gopher activity and make irrigation repairs and
adjustments throughout all City parks and City Hall.

The greens were fertilized at the Golf Course this quarter.

Staff planted 350 one gallon sized with a mixture of white and purple lantana plants on
the slope adjacent to the river to complete the Hollydale park project.

75 percent of the scheduled tree trimming at City Parks has been completed for this FY.

Staff continue servicing and beautifying over 190 acres of park land on a daily basis.

Park Facility Maintenance
Parks Facility Maintenance along with Grounds staff set up and hosted the State of The
City address in the Auditorium, The Art Walk at the Civic Center, and the Centennial
Car show in the Golf Course.

The Municipal Auditorium was renamed in honor of the late Henry C. Gonzales. The
project of installing the new name sign at the Auditorium and a plaque has been
completed.

Due to the high use of SG Park, Staff continues to do a third daily inspection and
cleaning, in the late afternoon to our outdoor restrooms.

  Page 1 of 2
  14
 We have continued the use of Electrostatic Disinfecting Equipment for more coverage in
our cleaning and disinfecting efforts for both indoor and outdoor restroom facilities,
along with a pressure washing program. These disinfecting and cleaning tools will be
used consistently. Set ups for all events require us to disinfect all tables, chairs, door
handles, and A/V equipment.

We are in full operation with classes, as well as private rentals, picnics, sports activities,
and service clubs’ events. We continue to host monthly food giveaways for the
community at two locations, one at Circle Park and one at Hollydale Regional Park.

The Community Service Worker program is ongoing; we are still limiting intake to 15
people maximum per day.

Parks are busy with many events, classes, picnics, and sports activities. Although
pandemic mandates have been lifted, we remain vigilant when addressing the ongoing
challenges with restroom cleanliness with a routine restroom disinfecting program. This
includes the use of the C3 Machine to apply disinfectants and cleaners. Once product is
sprayed, staff scrubs floors, walls, and fixtures to insure sanitary conditions.

  STAFF REPORT ITEM No. 4
To:  Honorable Parks & Recreation Commission
From:  Glenn Massey, Parks Superintendent
Date:  October 18, 2023

Subject:  Park Ranger and Executive Management Services Update

Recommended Motion:  Receive and file.

Report Summary: During the September Parks and Recreation Commission meeting,
Commissioner Pelayo requested a report regarding the Park Ranger and Security
Company be brought to the commission.

The Park Ranger program is supervised by the Parks Superintendent and is budgeted
for two full-time and four hourly positions. Currently we are understaffed as there is only
one (1) of the FT staff positions filled and one (1) on an “Acting” basis. We are just now
getting our first hourly position filled out of the four. The positions are held by
Community Service Officers (CSO) hired and trained by the Police Department. Once
their training is complete, they are transferred to work in the Park Ranger Program
providing routine observe and report patrol in all our parks. Along with this, they enforce
municipal codes and laws, including; dispatch calls from the police department,
answering questions and reports from park patrons, writing citations to vehicles and
persons committing unlawful acts and reporting deficiencies to park staff i.e.; graffiti,
missing signs, broken items, faulty irrigation and the like. When necessary, they request
assistance from police officers. They will also assist officers when dispatch sends
officers to respond to calls at parks. The typical schedule when we are fully staffed is
one working a morning shift, one an evening shift during the weekdays. During the
weekends we typically would schedule one or two based on the event schedule.

The goal of most of our CSO’s is to seek further employment as police officers or other
law enforcement careers. Usually, after a few years working as a CSO, these staff
members are hired by various police agencies. Since the pandemic there has been a
large staff turnover rate and the City has experienced difficulties finding candidates to fill
vacancies in large part because of the background requirements.

Due to the challenges filling the vacancies within the Park Ranger Program, staff
decided in April of this year to seek the services of Executive Management Services to

  Page 1 of 2
  16
 assist the Park Ranger Program until vacancies were filled. They assist with observing
and reporting matters to police dispatch, answering questions or responding to matters
from park patrons, and covering shifts that the park Rangers cannot fill. Since the
security company has been brought on board, park patrons have expressed their
appreciation stating that they have seen a decline in inappropriate behavior and
generally feel safer in the parks. The Park Rangers appreciate the security company
assisting them in covering shifts, making sure that gates are locked, and parks are
closed in the evening. As staff continue to fill the current Park Ranger vacancies, we
anticipate reducing the number of hours needed from the security company over the
next six to nine months.
